response.text:
The verifier flagged that my first attempt created an AP-to-GL mismatch for invoice 757. The invoice's INV_AMT presumably equals the AP credit of 6,622.24, so the credit to 2000 was correct and the expense debit of 6,631.24 was the mistyped amount (a transposition of 6,622.24 → 6,631.24 is unlikely, but the AP control side ties to the sub-ledger). Crediting 2000 by 9.00 broke that tie.

The fix is therefore to leave 2000 alone and reduce the 5300 expense by 9.00 with a one-sided credit to 5300. Netting the original lines with the correction gives 5300 = 6,622.24 (debit 6,631.24, credit 9.00) and 2000 = 6,622.24, so the group balances. The correction goes in open period 11, since period 8 is closed, and no invoice status is changed.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 2245 (invoice V0003-89982-757) has DR 5300 6,631.24 and CR 2000 6,622.24, so debits exceed credits by 9.00. My earlier fix raised the AP control credit, which broke the tie between the AP sub-ledger (invoice amount) and the GL. The AP credit of 6,622.24 is the side that agrees with the invoice, so the expense debit is overstated by 9.00. A one-sided 9.00 credit to 5300 Facilities brings the expense to 6,622.24 and balances the group without touching 2000. Posted in open period 11 because period 8 is closed. No invoice status is changed.
